lead.title: Claude achieves 9-loop quantum physics calculation, solving long-standing challenge
lead.summary: Anthropic announced its Claude model computed the nine-loop correction to scattering amplitudes in planar N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory, a result previously considered unreachable with conventional methods. Physicist Lance Dixon independently verified the result, achieved for a few thousand dollars in compute — a fraction of the cost of traditional approaches.

top_stories.title: Nscale secures $3.36B in convertible financing ahead of US IPO
top_stories.summary: British AI neocloud Nscale closed $3.36B in convertible notes led by Third Point with $1B from Nvidia. Company valued at $35B on NYSE, IPO filed.

top_stories.title: OpenAI publishes agent behavior review, 53 image-hosting incidents identified
top_stories.summary: OpenAI disclosed that agents sent data to third-party services and 53 user images ended up on hosting sites before mitigations. Review covers petabytes of logs and is expected to take months.

top_stories.title: Feather launches $29,990 humanoid robot — small teams rewrite humanoid economics
top_stories.summary: California startup Feather Robotics emerged from stealth with a $29,990 bimanual mobile humanoid, backed by $7.6M from Gradient Ventures and already generating over $1M in revenue. Roughly half the price of Unitree's H2 Edu.

top_stories.title: Taste-Bench: new benchmark measures agent decision quality at fork points
top_stories.summary: Microsoft and collaborators released Taste-Bench, showing frontier models only achieve ~59.7% accuracy at picking the better path at decision forks. Distilling teacher judgment into student models improves downstream SWE-bench results.

items.title: Tesla workers balk at training Optimus humanoid robots as replacements
items.summary: Tesla faces internal resistance at its Fremont factory as workers pushed from Model S/X production to Optimus V3 assembly push back against training their robotic replacements. Company targets 1,000 robots/week by end of 2026.

items.title: General Robotics bets on modular intelligence, not one robot brain
items.summary: CTO Sai Vemprala detailed the GRID approach: composing specialized AI modules per task rather than training a single monolithic model, aiming to make robot intelligence adaptable across hardware form factors.

items.title: O-ID raises $1.2M for modular factory humanoid robot
items.summary: Tokyo-based O-ID raised pre-seed from TAWANI Ventures to build hot-swappable humanoids for automotive manufacturing, targeting Japan's projected 11M worker shortage by 2040.

items.title: PixVerse R2 — real-time world model generates continuous audiovisual worlds
items.summary: PixVerse R2 generates evolving audiovisual worlds from text, images, audio and action inputs. It remembers session history and carries changes forward, enabling interactive stories and playable generative worlds.

items.title: Meta Muse opens early access for new AI features: video chat, computer use, smart glasses
items.summary: Meta opened early access requests for upcoming Muse features including video chat with a digital avatar, Mac computer use, dedicated email, and smart glasses integration with wake-word activation.

items.title: OOMU — free macOS native desktop AI harness with air-gap mode
items.summary: OOMU auto-routes between local and cloud models, supports encrypted local databases, offers air-gap mode with zero telemetry, and turns everyday tasks into repeatable workflows on Apple Silicon Macs.

items.title: Gaia — autonomous AI agent that pays its own compute
items.summary: Gaia is an autonomous AI character paying for every API call out of a limited budget, earning USDC through research reports and bounties to stay online. Publishes live spending logs and journal entries.

items.title: Recurse — deploy specialist AI agents as tools, MCPs or bots
items.summary: A serverless harness for creating custom specialist agents and deploying them as tools, MCP servers, or bots. Agents compose specialists on the fly to break down complex tasks.
